Computing in Urban Environments: A
Constrained Multi-Objective Approach
With Task-Adaptive Mechanism
Zexiong Wu , Qiqi Xie , Zhuoran Wang, Xumin Huang
, Chaoda Peng , Member, IEEE,
and Yuan Wu , Senior Member, IEEE
Abstract—With the increasing and multifaceted demands for
wireless communication in smart cities, uncrewed aerial vehicle
(UAV)-enabled mobile edge computing (MEC) systems have gar-
nered substantial interest due to their potential to enhance con-
nectivity and computational capabilities. In these systems, UAVs
are deployed to predetermined locations to establish communica-
tion with nearby user devices (UDs), thereby providing network
coverage and computational offloading services. Nevertheless, the
presence of complex urban terrains, including rough topographies
and dense buildings, results in significant path loss in UAV-to-UD
communication links and increases the risk of collisions during UAV
navigation, ultimately degrading the quality of service (QoS) and
compromising UAV operational safety. To mitigate these challenges,
this study introduces a terrain-aware channel model capable of
precisely evaluating the effects of terrain characteristics on UAV-
to-UD link performance. To improve QoS for UDs while ensuring
UAV flight safety, we formulate a constrained multi-objective op-
timization problem (CMOP) to jointly optimize UAV trajectory,
destination, and resource allocation, aiming to minimize task com-
pletion time and enhance UAV flight safety. To solve this CMOP,
we propose a multi-task constrained multi-objective evolutionary
algorithm with a task-adaptive mechanism, promoting the search
for Pareto optimal solutions. Numerical results indicate that the
proposed method outperforms baseline algorithms in achieving a
well-converged set of feasible solutions with enhanced diversity.

formulate a constrained multi-objective optimization problem

finding a set of Pareto optimal solutions while satisfying all
constraints [22]. Evolutionary algorithms are popular choices
for addressing various CMOPs and have been widely applied
across numerous domains due to their inherent advantages,
such as ease of implementation and robust global optimization
capabilities [23]. The overall performance of these algorithms
significantly depends on the selection of genetic operators, since
these operators are crucial for effectively finding Pareto optimal
solutions [24]. To tackle the CMOP studied in this paper, we

ary algorithm (CMOEA) with a task-adaptive mechanism to
seek superior solutions. The main contributions of this paper

We propose a UAV-enabled MEC system tailored for com-
plex urban terrains. In this system, a UAV departs from an
initial position and flies to a final destination, providing
offloading services to nearby UDs. To accurately estimate
the signal strength, we design a terrain-aware channel
model. Unlike existing blockage-aware channel models
that assume simple terrains with flat topographies, our
proposed model can identify blockages caused by complex
terrains. This capability makes it applicable to a wider
range of urban environments, offering greater flexibility
and broader applicability.
- We study a CMOP by jointly optimizing UAV flight tra-
jectory, destination, and resource allocation. This joint
optimization ensures reduced task completion time while
enhancing safety on complex urban terrains.
We propose a multi-tasking CMOEA with a task-adaptive
mechanism. This mechanism can retain historically ef-
fective genetic operators and adaptively assigns different
genetic operators to individuals based on their specific
tasks during the evolution process, thereby enhancing the
search capability and convergence performance of the pro-
posed algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that our
algorithm significantly outperforms baseline algorithms in
terms of solution diversity and convergence.

A. Path Loss Channel Models
In this subsection, existing path loss channel models are clas-
sified into three distinct categories based on their methodological
approaches for inferring propagation conditions and estimating
average signal strength.
Statistical models are commonly used to assess the average
performance of communication channels [14]. These models
characterize propagation conditions using empirical channel
parameters obtained from statistical measurements. Given spe-
cific channel parameters and a UAV-UD position pair, they
can directly estimate the average signal strength. For example,
probabilistic LoS channel models that incorporate parameters
related to LoS and NLoS conditions have been utilized to
predict the average signal strength of UAV-to-UD links [11],
[25]. These models are widely applied in hierarchical comput-
ing frameworks, where the next-generation wireless networks
(6G) are leveraged to aggregate substantial computational re-
sources to process the time-varying multi-modal data uploaded
by UDs [26], [27]. However, these simplified statistical channel
models are only suitable for analyzing average performance
and may fail to provide satisfactory results for specific user
equipments (UEs) in real-world environments [13]. In practice,
terrain conditions such as buildings and other obstacles can
obstruct air-to-ground (A2G) signals, significantly degrading
the propagation environment, particularly in densely built urban
areas [13].

Radio map-based channel models can accurately assess the
impact of obstacles on signals and describe the average strength
of UAV-to-UD signals [14]. These models require extensive
channel measurement data to create a radio map using machine
learning techniques. The goal is to train a channel predictor that
determines the propagation conditions and estimates the signal
strength for the UAV-to-UD link [13], [28]. In [28], a predictor
for radio map reconstruction is developed by employing the
K-Nearest Neighbor algorithm to learn segments. Given a spe-
cific UAV-to-UD position pair, the trained predictor utilizes the
radio map to determine the propagation conditions and estimate
the signal strength. However, due to the difficulty of obtaining
sufficiently accurate channel quality assessments for possible
combinations of UAV-UE 3-D positions, practical applications
of radio maps are challenging [14].
Geographic information-based channel models can identify
LoS/NLoS conditions and predict the average signal strength by
evaluating A2G links obstructed by buildings [14]. These models
can construct a blocked region for a UD by using basic geometric
principles and geographic information [15]. By computing the
distance between UAV and blocked region, the propagation
conditions and signal strength can be inferred. Particularly,
when a UAV hovers outside the blocked region, the distance
between UAV and blocked region is positive, which can judge
the propagation conditions as LoS. In [29], a distance-based
weighted sum method is designed to improve the estimation
performance of blockage-aware channel models by exploiting
the fine-grained structure of propagation conditions. However,
these studies typically assume a simple urban terrain with flat
topography. In practical urban scenarios, rough topography can
significantly affect the signal strength of UAV-to-UD links [30].
B. Trajectory Design for UAV Flight Safety
In this subsection, we categorize the existing methods for
designing UAV flight trajectories into two distinct groups based
on their approaches to achieving safe flight paths.
Several studies have focused on obtaining collision-free UAV
flight trajectories by restricting the UAV flight area [15], [31].
In [32], an optimization problem is formulated to minimize task
completion time while satisfying the minimum data demand of
each user, under the assumption that the minimum flight altitude
of the UAV exceeds the height of the tallest buildings. In [33],
the flight area was predefined to ensure UAV flight safety near
buildings. Following this, a joint optimization of transmission
power, computation frequency, and duration is performed to
minimize UAV energy consumption and task completion time.
However, the assumption of a restricted UAV flight region in
these studies can sacrifice potential low-altitude collision-free
flight trajectories.
Some research incorporates UAV flight safety as an optimiza-
tion objective or constraint to achieve collision-free UAV flight
paths [34]. In [16], [34], collision avoidance constraints are used
to ensure that the distance between the UAV and buildings is
greater than a predefined value, resulting in a safe UAV flight
trajectory. In [20], an optimization objective that represents the
number of potential threatening terrain points near the UAV
is constructed. By optimizing this objective while considering
UAV dynamic constraints regarding turning angle, feasible so-
lutions can be obtained to form safe and smooth UAV flight
trajectories. However, these studies typically assume predefined
initial and final positions for the UAV flight. In practical urban
scenarios, the location of the UAV destination can also affect
flight safety.
C. Critical Analysis of the Literature Review
Based on the above analyses of existing research, we identify
two critical challenges in current UAV-enabled MEC systems.
First, existing path loss channel models exhibit limited appli-
cability in complex urban environments due to their reliance
on extensive data collection or oversimplified terrain assump-
tions. Second, while various approaches have been proposed
for UAV trajectory optimization, the impact of destination se-
lection on both communication performance and flight safety
remains largely unexplored. To address these challenges, we pro-
pose a comprehensive solution framework. For accurate signal
strength estimation, we develop a terrain-aware approach uti-
lizing real-world data, which systematically constructs blocked
regions through an iterative integration process. To enhance both
communication efficiency and operational safety, we design
a safety-enhanced flight model based on the B-spline curve,
enabling joint optimization of UAV trajectory and destination.
These innovations lay the foundation for our subsequent problem
formulation and algorithm design, which will be detailed in the
following sections.

determines the propagation conditions and estimates the signal
strength for the UAV-to-UD link [13], [28]. In [28], a predictor
for radio map reconstruction is developed by employing the
K-Nearest Neighbor algorithm to learn segments. Given a spe-
cific UAV-to-UD position pair, the trained predictor utilizes the
radio map to determine the propagation conditions and estimate
the signal strength. However, due to the difficulty of obtaining
sufficiently accurate channel quality assessments for possible
combinations of UAV-UE 3-D positions, practical applications
of radio maps are challenging [14].
Geographic information-based channel models can identify
LoS/NLoS conditions and predict the average signal strength by
evaluating A2G links obstructed by buildings [14]. These models
can construct a blocked region for a UD by using basic geometric
principles and geographic information [15]. By computing the
distance between UAV and blocked region, the propagation
conditions and signal strength can be inferred. Particularly,
when a UAV hovers outside the blocked region, the distance
between UAV and blocked region is positive, which can judge
the propagation conditions as LoS. In [29], a distance-based
weighted sum method is designed to improve the estimation
performance of blockage-aware channel models by exploiting
the fine-grained structure of propagation conditions. However,
these studies typically assume a simple urban terrain with flat
topography. In practical urban scenarios, rough topography can
significantly affect the signal strength of UAV-to-UD links [30].
B. Trajectory Design for UAV Flight Safety
In this subsection, we categorize the existing methods for
designing UAV flight trajectories into two distinct groups based
on their approaches to achieving safe flight paths.
Several studies have focused on obtaining collision-free UAV
flight trajectories by restricting the UAV flight area [15], [31].
In [32], an optimization problem is formulated to minimize task
completion time while satisfying the minimum data demand of
each user, under the assumption that the minimum flight altitude
of the UAV exceeds the height of the tallest buildings. In [33],
the flight area was predefined to ensure UAV flight safety near
buildings. Following this, a joint optimization of transmission
power, computation frequency, and duration is performed to
minimize UAV energy consumption and task completion time.
However, the assumption of a restricted UAV flight region in
these studies can sacrifice potential low-altitude collision-free
flight trajectories.
Some research incorporates UAV flight safety as an optimiza-
tion objective or constraint to achieve collision-free UAV flight
paths [34]. In [16], [34], collision avoidance constraints are used
to ensure that the distance between the UAV and buildings is
greater than a predefined value, resulting in a safe UAV flight
trajectory. In [20], an optimization objective that represents the
number of potential threatening terrain points near the UAV
is constructed. By optimizing this objective while considering
UAV dynamic constraints regarding turning angle, feasible so-
lutions can be obtained to form safe and smooth UAV flight
trajectories. However, these studies typically assume predefined
initial and final positions for the UAV flight. In practical urban
scenarios, the location of the UAV destination can also affect
flight safety.
C. Critical Analysis of the Literature Review
Based on the above analyses of existing research, we identify
two critical challenges in current UAV-enabled MEC systems.
First, existing path loss channel models exhibit limited appli-
cability in complex urban environments due to their reliance
on extensive data collection or oversimplified terrain assump-
tions. Second, while various approaches have been proposed
for UAV trajectory optimization, the impact of destination se-
lection on both communication performance and flight safety
remains largely unexplored. To address these challenges, we pro-
pose a comprehensive solution framework. For accurate signal
strength estimation, we develop a terrain-aware approach uti-
lizing real-world data, which systematically constructs blocked
regions through an iterative integration process. To enhance both
communication efficiency and operational safety, we design
a safety-enhanced flight model based on the B-spline curve,
enabling joint optimization of UAV trajectory and destination.
These innovations lay the foundation for our subsequent problem
formulation and algorithm design, which will be detailed in the
following sections.

C. Investigation of the Task-Adaptive Mechanism
To evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed task-adaptive
mechanism, we conduct comparative experiments on CMOP2
using two algorithm configurations: one incorporating the task-
adaptive mechanism (denoted as “Yes”) and another using the
original genetic operators (denoted as “No”). The original ge-
netic operators utilize the DE/current-to-rand/1 operator and
polynomial mutation. Table IV presents the comparative re-
sults, demonstrating the significant impact of the task-adaptive
mechanism.
Our task-adaptive mechanism significantly enhances algo-
rithm performance through genetic operator coordination. This
mechanism intelligently selects and applies genetic operators
based on historical performance data, dynamically matching
operators to specific solution characteristics. Through experi-
mental validation, we demonstrate its effectiveness with a 19.0%
reduction in mean IGD value and a 32.2% increase in mean HV
value compared to the original genetic operators. The mech-
anism achieves an optimal balance between exploration and
exploitation through three complementary mutation operators:
the first creates smoother trajectories by enhancing similarity
between control points, the second explores potential feasible
trajectories through strategic randomized control point genera-
tion, and the third applies polynomial mutation with precisely
controlled perturbations to navigate the solution space effi-
ciently. By recording and reapplying effective genetic operators
that worked well on similar individuals, the proposed algorithm
effectively balances between discovering promising solution
regions and refining solutions in these areas, thereby enhancing
its capabilities in balancing flight safety and communication
efficiency requirements.

that dynamically assigns genetic operators based on solution

exploitation through three complementary mutation operators:
the first creates smoother trajectories by enhancing similarity
between control points, the second explores potential feasible
trajectories through strategic randomized control point genera-
tion, and the third applies polynomial mutation with precisely
controlled perturbations to navigate the solution space effi-
ciently. By recording and reapplying effective genetic operators
that worked well on similar individuals, the proposed algorithm
effectively balances between discovering promising solution
regions and refining solutions in these areas, thereby enhancing
its capabilities in balancing flight safety and communication
efficiency requirements.
VI. CONCLUSION
In this study, we investigated a UAV-enabled MEC system
operating in complex urban environments, where rough topogra-
phies and dense buildings pose significant challenges to both
UAV-to-UD communication links and flight safety. Our contri-
butions are threefold: First, we proposed a terrain-aware channel
model that effectively evaluates the impact of complex urban
terrain on UAV communication performance by systematically
constructing blocked regions through an iterative integration
process. Second, we formulated a CMOP that jointly optimizes
UAV trajectory, destination position, and resource allocation to
balance QoS enhancement and flight safety. Third, we devel-
oped a multi-tasking CMOEA with a task-adaptive mechanism
that dynamically assigns genetic operators based on solution
characteristics.
Our comprehensive experimental results demonstrated the
superior performance of the proposed algorithm across three test
scenarios of increasing complexity, achieving approximately
70.2% reduction in mean IGD and 77.5% increase in mean HV
compared to baseline algorithms. The ablation studies validated
the effectiveness of our task-adaptive mechanism, which im-
proved performance by 19.0% in IGD and 32.2% in HV by
intelligently leveraging historical information about effective
genetic operators. Additionally, our terrain-aware channel model
proved significantly more accurate than the probabilistic LoS
channel model, achieving practical LoS probabilities of 95.63%
compared to 63.45% with traditional approaches.

Macau, Macau, SAR, China, and also with the
Department of Computer and Information Science,
University of Macau. His research interests include
resource management for wireless networks, mo-
bile edge computing and edge intelligence, inte-
grated sensing and communications. He was the
recipient of the Best Paper Award from the IEEE
ICC’2016, IEEE TCGCC’2017, IWCMC’2021, and
IEEE WCNC’2023. Dr. Wu is on the editorial board of IEEE TRANSACTIONS
ON VEHICULAR TECHNOLOGY, IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON NETWORK SCIENCE
AND ENGINEERING, and IEEE INTERNET OF THINGS JOURNAL. He is the Distin-
guished Lecturer of IEEE Vehicular Technology Society.
